name: Scenario I: Payment Failure & Dunning
description: Triggers on Stripe payment_intent.payment_failed (and invoice.payment_failed). Parses the failure, fetches the customer from Stripe, finds the HubSpot contact, logs a note, alerts Brian internally via Resend (from env.CWI_ALERT_FROM_ADDRESS to env.ADMIN_EMAIL), and sends a friendly white-labeled card-update email to the client via Resend (from env.RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS) linking to the Stripe customer portal. CWI AI is never mentioned in the client-facing email.
comments: STRIPE WEBHOOK VERIFICATION NOTE: Make.com's Stripe webhook module automatically validates the Stripe-Signature header using your configured Stripe webhook signing secret (HMAC-SHA256). Enter the signing secret from Stripe Dashboard (Developers > Webhooks > your endpoint > Signing secret) in the Stripe module connection. Do NOT expose this secret in code or logs. DUNNING NOTE: This scenario handles both payment_intent.payment_failed and invoice.payment_failed. The BasicFeeder (module 2) normalizes both event shapes into a single set of fields so all downstream modules are object-agnostic. To handle both event types in production, create two webhook endpoints (one per event type) pointing at the same scenario, or use a single endpoint subscribed to both events. WHITE-LABEL NOTE: The client-facing email (module 9) MUST send from env.RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS (the client's own verified domain) and MUST NOT reference CWI AI, brian@cwiai.net, or any CWI branding. All secrets are referenced via env.VARIABLE_NAME and never hardcoded.

hookName.label: CWI Stripe Webhook — payment_intent.payment_failed OR invoice.payment_failed

metadata.note: Instant trigger. Fires on Stripe payment_intent.payment_failed. For invoice.payment_failed, subscribe the same endpoint to both events in the Stripe Dashboard — module 2 normalizes both payload shapes. Signature verification is handled automatically by Make using the configured webhook signing secret.

mapper.failure_reason: {{ifempty(1.data.object.last_payment_error.message, ifempty(1.data.object.failure_message, 'Payment was declined. No failure reason provided by Stripe.'))}}

metadata.note: Step 1: Parse Stripe webhook payload. Normalizes payment_intent.payment_failed and invoice.payment_failed into one shape: customer_id, amount (cents->dollars), currency, failure_reason, failure_code, invoice_id, payment_intent_id. Dates formatted in America/New_York (Eastern Time).
Step 2: GET https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers/{{customer_id}} to retrieve the customer's name and email for the HubSpot lookup and both emails. Uses env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (restricted read key).

Step 3: POST https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/contacts/search to find the HubSpot contact by the email returned from Stripe (module 3). Returns the contact id used to associate the note in step 4.

Step 4: POST https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/notes. Logs note 'Payment failed — {date} — {amount} — Reason: {failure_reason}' associated with the contact found in step 3. associationTypeId 202 = Contact-to-Note.

Step 5: Internal alert to Brian. POST https://api.resend.com/emails. FROM env.CWI_ALERT_FROM_ADDRESS, TO env.ADMIN_EMAIL. Subject 'PAYMENT FAILED — [client name] — $[amount]'. Body includes full details and Stripe dashboard links.

Step 6: Friendly client-facing card-update email. POST https://api.resend.com/emails. FROM env.RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS (client's own verified domain). TO the client's email from Stripe. White-labeled: does NOT mention CWI AI or any CWI branding. Links to env.STRIPE_CUSTOMER_PORTAL_URL.

Step 7: Error handler covering modules 2-7. Catches any failure (Stripe fetch, HubSpot search/note, internal alert, or client email) and notifies env.ADMIN_EMAIL via Resend from env.CWI_ALERT_FROM_ADDRESS with all known details, Stripe link, the error message, and the failed module for fast manual remediation. Timestamp in America/New_York.

stripe.label: CWI Stripe Connection
stripe.note: Requires Stripe API key (restricted key with customer read + webhook read access) and the webhook signing secret for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification.

setupInstructions.step1_stripe_webhook: In Stripe Dashboard: Developers > Webhooks > Add endpoint. Point it at your Make.com webhook URL. Subscribe to BOTH event types: payment_intent.payment_failed AND invoice.payment_failed. Copy the Signing Secret into the Stripe module connection in Make.com. Module 2 (BasicFeeder) normalizes both payload shapes so all downstream modules are object-agnostic.
setupInstructions.step2_stripe_api_key: Set env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to a restricted Stripe key with read access to Customers (used by GET /v1/customers/{id} in module 3).
setupInstructions.step3_hubspot_scopes: Create a HubSpot Private App with scopes: crm.objects.contacts.read and crm.objects.notes.write. Store the access token in env.HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN. Modules 4-5 search the contact by email and log a payment-failure note (associationTypeId 202 = Contact-to-Note).
setupInstructions.step4_resend: Set env.RESEND_API_KEY. Set env.CWI_ALERT_FROM_ADDRESS (verified CWI sender) for internal alerts and the error handler. Set env.RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS to the CLIENT's own verified Resend domain for the white-labeled client email. Set env.ADMIN_EMAIL to brian@cwiai.net (or the owner inbox). The client-facing email MUST NOT mention CWI AI.
setupInstructions.step5_customer_portal: Set env.STRIPE_CUSTOMER_PORTAL_URL to your Stripe Customer Portal login URL (Stripe Dashboard > Settings > Billing > Customer portal). The client email links here so customers can self-serve a card update; Stripe auto-retries the payment afterward.
setupInstructions.step6_testing: Test with Stripe CLI: stripe trigger payment_intent.payment_failed and stripe trigger invoice.payment_failed. Confirm: (1) Stripe customer fetched, (2) HubSpot contact found + note logged, (3) internal alert reaches env.ADMIN_EMAIL from env.CWI_ALERT_FROM_ADDRESS, (4) client email sends from env.RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS with no CWI branding and a working portal link.
